name: Treaty of Mendota (1851)
aka: Treaty with the Sioux-Mdewakanton and Wahpakoota Bands, 1851
promises: $1,410,000 in all for the bands' lands and claims in Minnesota Territory and Iowa (Articles 2 and 4).
$220,000 to the chiefs for debts and a year's support after removal, and $30,000 for manual-labour schools, mills, blacksmith shops and farming (Article 4).

$1,160,000 held in trust with five per cent interest paid for fifty years from July 1, 1852, for an agricultural and civilization fund, education, goods and provisions, and a money annuity (Article 4), and the 1837 treaty annuity paid in money (Article 5).

Article 3, a reservation on the Minnesota River, was struck out by the Senate; the supplemental article paid ten cents an acre for it instead and let the President, with the bands' consent, mark out another home outside the cession.

breaches.what: After the 1862 war in Minnesota, Congress declared all treaties with the Sisseton, Wahpeton, Mdewakanton and Wahpekute bands abrogated and annulled so far as they imposed any future obligation on the United States, and declared their lands and rights of occupancy in Minnesota and their annuities and claims forfeited, appropriating two thirds of the unexpended annuities for damages claims.

source.title: An Act for the Relief of Persons for Damages sustained by Reason of Depredations and Injuries by certain Bands of Sioux Indians, 12 Stat. 652 (February 16, 1863)

breaches.quote: are hereby declared to be abrogated and annulled

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission held in 1962 that the Mdewakanton and Wahpekute (Docket 362) had recognised title to Royce Area 289 as of this treaty; their claims and those of the Sisseton and Wahpeton, except a general accounting claim in Docket 363, were settled by a stipulated compromise in 1967 for final judgments in the net amount of $12,250,000 across Dockets 142 and 359-363.

breaches.what: The Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community's history timeline records, under 1862, that no annuity payments were made to the Mdewakanton, which it calls an indication of clear breaches of treaty rights.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community, Our History timeline

breaches.what: The Lower Sioux Indian Community states that the United States failed for two years before August 1862 to meet its treaty obligations, including payment for the land, health care and food, and afterwards nullified its treaties with the Dakota, voided their annuities and removed them from Minnesota.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Lower Sioux Indian Community, About Us and History of the Mdewakanton

landTaken: Royce Area 289, ceded jointly by this treaty and the Traverse des Sioux treaty (kappler-596). The acreage was not copied here.
compensation: The 1863 act forfeited the unpaid annuities. The Indian Claims Commission claims of the four bands for the 1851 cessions and other dockets were compromised in 1967 for a net $12,250,000.
today: Descendants include the Lower Sioux Indian Community, Prairie Island Indian Community, Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community, Upper Sioux Community, Santee Sioux Nation and Flandreau Santee Sioux Tribe, as listed in the queue for this cession.

plain.promised: $1,410,000 for the bands' lands in Minnesota Territory and Iowa, including money for debts, schools and farming, with $1,160,000 held in trust paying five per cent interest for fifty years.
plain.happened: After the 1862 war, Congress in 1863 annulled the treaties and declared the annuities forfeited. The Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community records that no annuities were paid to the Mdewakanton in 1862, a clear breach.
plain.today: Indian Claims Commission claims for the 1851 cessions and other dockets were compromised in 1967 for a net $12,250,000. Whether that was paid has not been traced.

nationVoice.summary: The Community's history says the two 1851 treaties, Traverse des Sioux and Mendota, had the four Dakota bands give up over 30 million acres in Minnesota Territory and Iowa for money and a permanent reservation on the Minnesota River, and that by 1862 no annuity payments were being made to the Mdewakanton, a clear breach of treaty rights.

nationVoice.nation: Lower Sioux Indian Community (Mdewakanton Band of Dakota)
nationVoice.summary: The Community says 'Lower Sioux' was the name given to its band and homeland after the 1851 treaties, that the 1862 war followed two years of unfulfilled treaty obligations including unpaid land money, health care and food, and that the United States then nullified its treaties, voided the annuities and removed the Dakota from Minnesota.

openQuestions: The 1863 act's preamble gives Congress's reasons in its own words (the 1862 war); the record states the act's effect only.

Medawakanton and Wahpakoota Bands v. United States, 57 Ct. Cl. 357 (1922), on the partial restoration of the forfeited annuities, was not opened; it is the main lead for a court finding on this treaty.
The Senate's amendment striking the Article 3 reservation, and how the bands' assent to it was obtained, is a lead for a deeper pass.
No account of this treaty by a Dakota nation was located in this pass.

Audit 2026-11-08: treaty articles, the 1863 act and the ICC orders checked. The litigation text drops the unsourced 'without a finding on the price' and notes the Docket 363 exclusion; the Shakopee statement is reworded to the timeline's own phrasing. The note that no Dakota account was located is out of date: Shakopee and Lower Sioux pages are cited.
